talia: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind; tālia, such things, such words (n. acc./nom. pl.)
tandem: tandem (adv.) — at length, finally; in questions, pray, I ask
tanti: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (m. nom. pl.; n. gen. sg.)
tantum: tantus, -a, -um — so great; tantum (n. acc. sg.), so great a thing; (adv.) only, so much · also m. acc. sg. (tantum dolorem)
tempora: tempus, temporis (n.) — time, season, occasion (acc. pl.) · also tempora, -um (n. pl.), temples of the head (acc. pl.)
tendere: tendō, -ere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, direct one's course, make for (pres. inf.)
tenebat: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, grasp (3rd sg. impf.)
tenebris: tenebrae, -ārum (f. pl.) — darkness, gloom, shadows (abl./dat. pl.)
tenuere: teneō, tenēre, tenuī — to hold, occupy, keep (3rd pl. perf., = tenuērunt)
terra: terra, -ae (f.) — land, earth, ground (nom./abl. sg.) · also f. voc. sg. (ō terra hospita)
teucrorum: Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Teucrians, Trojans (from Teucer, an early king of Troy) (gen. pl.)
thybrim: Thybris, -idis (m.) — the Tiber (acc. sg., Greek form in -im)
totidem: totidem (indecl. adj.) — just as many, the same number
traxit: trahō, -ere, trāxī, tractum — to drag, draw (3rd sg. perf.)
triste: tristis, -e — grim, sad, bitter (n. acc. sg.)
troia: Trōius, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (abl. sg., from Troy) · also nom. sg., Troy (servātaque serves Trōia fidem)
troïa: Trōius, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (n. acc. pl.; f. nom. sg.), with diaeresis ï
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tumulum: tumulus, -ī (m.) — mound, hillock, burial mound (acc. sg.)
ulla: ūllus, -a, -um — any (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.); with non, no
ultro: ultrō (adv.) — of one's own accord, voluntarily; besides
undique: undique (adv.) — from all sides, on every side
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
valet: valeō, -ēre, -uī — to be strong, have power, be able (3rd sg. pres.)
varios: varius, -a, -um — various, diverse, changing (m. acc. pl.)
velis: vēlum, -ī (n.) — sail; canvas, cloth, awning (abl./dat. pl.) · also volō, velle, voluī — to wish (2nd sg. pres. subj.: esse velīs)
velit: volō, velle, voluī — to wish, want, be willing (3rd sg. pres. subj.)
venti: ventus, -ī (m.) — wind (nom. pl.; gen. sg.) · also voc. pl., in address (sine nūmine, ventī)
ventum: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (perf. pass. part., n. sg., in impersonal ventum est, they came)
vertice: vertex, verticis (m.) — peak, summit; whirl (abl. sg.)
veterum: vetus, veteris — old, ancient, long-standing (gen. pl.)
viribus: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, strength; pl. vīrēs, vīrium, strength (abl./dat. pl.)
viscera: viscus, vīsceris (n.) — flesh; pl. viscera, entrails (acc. pl.)
visu: vīsus, -ūs (m.) — sight, seeing (abl. sg.; miserābile vīsū, pitiable to see)
vobis: tū, tuī — you; vōs, vōbīs, to/for you, by you (dat./abl. pl.)
vocabat: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, summon, invite (3rd sg. imperf.)
vocat: vocō, -āre — to call, name, summon (3rd sg. pres.)
vota: vōtum, -ī (n.) — vow, promise to a god, prayer (acc./nom. pl.)
